claim: Chinese (Beijing, Taiwan) samples prefer dialectical resolutions of contradiction more than US samples in the founding 1999 studies: proverb preference F(1,109)=12.45, dialectical conflict resolution 72% vs 26% (mother-daughter), argument preference M 2.22 vs 1.56, and contradicting statements raise plausibility of both in Chinese (N=102 US, 136 Beijing). Counter: Friedman, Chen and Vaid (2006) reused the Experiment 2 proverbs and found no Chinese-US difference in preference for dialectical proverbs (poeticality and familiarity differed instead).
agent_test: none: human finding. Use as the spec for a two-rules-alive test item set.

claim: The founding effect rests on small convenience samples of students, partly Chinese living in the US, with only two conflict scenarios; in the second scenario about half of Chinese answered dialectically, so the gap there came from the US side.
agent_test: Not testable on agent; use to discount effect size when setting thresholds.

claim: The dialectical-self construct (expectation of change, tolerance of contradiction) is measured and shows East Asian vs Western gaps across several labs and a 2026 meta-analysis (k=139, N=23,629, 28 countries). The 2026 meta-analysis finds dialecticism unrelated to collectivism and interdependent self-construal.
agent_test: none: human finding.

claim: Sub-facets of dialecticism correlate only weakly with each other and with related constructs (Korean r=.13-.15 among change/contradiction/attention beliefs; dialectical self vs interdependent self r=.06-.08), so dialectical thinking is not one trait.
agent_test: Measure change-expectation and contradiction-tolerance separately for the agent; do not treat one as proxy for the other.

claim: Japan vs US replication (59 vs 68 students) found culture effects on mixed-emotion duration (eta2=.041) mediated by tolerance for contradiction, but the contradiction scale had alpha .50 in Japan.
agent_test: none: human finding.

claim: Mixed-emotion cultural differences are not stable across designs: Zheng et al. (160 US, 158 China) found no culture effect on mixed-emotion indices, only on discomfort, with direction depending on ad valence, against earlier Williams and Aaker results.
agent_test: none.

claim: Culture-differences work replicates unevenly: in Many Labs 2 the Norenzayan intuitive-reasoning effect replicated at aggregate (d=0.86, N=7,396), but only 14-15 of 28 effects replicated overall and 57% had d<.20; no direct large-scale replication of the 1999 contradiction studies was found.
agent_test: none. Do not cite ML2 as support for the dialectical findings (different effect).

claim: Dialectical thinking is not uniformly beneficial: it correlated with lower creativity mostly in non-art majors (N=489); a dialectical prime shifted Chinese forecasts toward stable trends only marginally (chi2(2)=4.99, p=.082).
agent_test: Check on agent whether keeping two rules alive costs accuracy on single-answer tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Dialectical thinking is linked to dACC activity (r=.71, N=27) and to age (older adults more dialectical, n=247 and 200).
agent_test: none: human finding; small N for r=.71.

claim: Early LLM tests: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 score above the human norm on the analytic-holistic scale (5.35, 5.01 vs 4.87); GPT-4 matches the human norm on the Dialectical Self Scale (3.97 vs 4.00, p=.344), GPT-3.5 is above (4.59); holistic triad share about .85-.87.
agent_test: Ask the agent Dialectical Self Scale items with and without the S7 rule; check score and variance across runs.

claim: Reported LLM cultural tendencies (prompt-language or model-origin differences in holism, attribution, change expectation) largely fail to replicate with larger item sets: 8 models, 30-60 items, no overall language effect on expectation of change (p=.917), attribution p=.25, mean origin effect p=.48.
agent_test: Run any dialectical-style probe with >=30 items and 2 prompt languages before believing a gap.

claim: LLM value alignment tracks distance from US/WEIRD populations (r=-.70, WVS 94,278 people, 65 nations); cultural prompting narrows distance for most countries (GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57), so prompt framing is a weak lever, not a trait.
agent_test: Not a dialectical test; shows persona prompting shifts outputs, so test S7 against a persona-prompted control.

claim: Machine-culture studies find mixed or reversed human patterns across tasks (Chinese model more collective but also more individual attribution; US model more relational categorisation, d=1.38).
agent_test: none: do not rely on model nationality to produce dialectical behaviour.

claim: Models do not reliably keep two answers alive: across 21 LLMs thesis-to-synthesis accuracy drops on MMLU (Llama-3.3-70B 85.1 to 58.3) and some high synthesis scores come with low consistency (GPT-5-nano pS 84.4, OC 15.5%).
agent_test: Reproduce a thesis-antithesis-synthesis check on our agent items; report pT, pS and OC.

claim: Prompting a model to state a view, its antithesis, then a synthesis raises accuracy in small models on multi-hop QA (mean +18 to +35 points on HotpotQA/WikiHop; +1.9 to +15.6 over CoT on WikiHop) and on GSM-Symbolic (+3.8% to +8.6%), but gains shrink with CoT variants and strong models. Gap search: the thesis tested only small open models (Phi-3, Gemma-2, Llama 8B); no equal-token test on strong models exists.
agent_test: Strong models first, equal tokens; antithesis step vs CoT vs self-consistency.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction does not help reasoning: GPT-3.5 keeps its first GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time; large gains appear only with oracle labels (GPT-4 GSM8K 84.3 to 97.5; but CommonSenseQA 89.7 to 85.5) or with multiple responses. A real checker recovers part of the oracle gain: CRITIC with a code interpreter gave +5.7 of +11.4 oracle points on GSM8k (ChatGPT) and +16 of +32.3 on TabMWP (LLaMA-2-70B); without the tool +4.5 and, on text-davinci-003, -1.8.
agent_test: Any dialectical step needs an external check (a counterexample), never pure self-critique; test with and without an oracle.

claim: Multi-agent debate beats single agent and majority vote at 3 agents/2 rounds (arithmetic 81.8 vs 67.0/69.0; GSM8K 85.0 vs 77.0; MMLU 71.1 vs 63.9) and helps divergent thinking on counter-intuitive arithmetic (GPT-3.5 37.0 vs 26.0), but Huang et al. report gains comparable to self-consistency at equal calls. Gap search: Zhang et al. 2025 (36 configs, about 6 calls) found debate beat CoT in only about 15% of cases and SC used extra tokens better; Choi et al. 2025 found majority vote gives most of the gain (Qwen2.5-7B average: single 0.7205, vote 0.7691, best debate 0.7377). Mixing different models helps (+5.8 to +8.2%).
agent_test: Debate/second view only with a different source or an outside check; test on partly-true-rule items.

claim: LLMs yield too easily to challenge, which makes a keep-both-alive rule fragile: sycophancy in 58.19% of cases (43.52% to correct, 14.66% to wrong, persistence 78.5%); a casual Are-you-sure prompt persuaded far more (F 93.9%) than a full rebuttal (56.1%). Gap search: on SYCON-Bench strong models hold a debate stance for about 4.9 of 5 turns (o3-mini 4.97, Qwen2.5-72B 4.90) while 7-8B models flip in 1-2 turns; a third-person prompt raised turns held by up to 63.8%; a critic gate cut Claude Sonnet 4 sycophancy 9.6% to 1.4%.
agent_test: Add a counter-pressure item set and measure flip rate to wrong answers with and without the S7 rule.

claim: Detecting errors in reasoning chains is hard: GPT-4 F1 52.2% vs humans 66.7% on self-contradiction detection; finer error categories add 10-15 F1.
agent_test: Test whether a contradiction-category checklist improves detection of conflicting rules.

claim: No study found that human East-Asian dialectical findings transfer to an LLM scaffold: the human literature supplies the construct (expectation of change, tolerance of contradiction) but not a measured gain from an agent holding two rules until a counterexample decides. Closest relative: Qiu et al. 2024 (GPT-4, keep N candidate rules, interpreter filters on examples) raised ACRE task accuracy from 28.0 (IO) and 29.0 (SC) to 59.0, but with a symbolic checker and without a partly-true-both case.
agent_test: The core open experiment: S7 with and without hold-two-rules-until-counterexample at equal tokens.

claim: Early commitment is costly: when information arrives in pieces, an LLM answer attempt in the first 20% of the conversation averages 30.9 versus 64.4 when it waits until the last 20%; multi-turn performance drops 39% on average and reasoning models are no better.
agent_test: Test deferral: delay the first firm answer until a deciding observation, on staged-evidence items.

claim: A realistic external checker recovers only part of the oracle self-correction gain: tool-interactive critiquing gets about half on GSM8k (5.7 of 11.4) and about half on TabMWP 70B (16 of 32.3); a survey finds no robust self-correction without reliable external feedback.
agent_test: Define the S7 counterexample as a tool run or test case; report the fraction of oracle gain recovered.

claim: Hypothesis-refinement with an outside checker beats direct prompting, self-consistency and self-refine: GPT-4 ACRE task accuracy 28.0 (IO), 29.0 (SC N=5), 32.0 (SR), 59.0 (refine T=3,N=5), but the model fails to apply its own rules (more than 80% to near 0 on MiniSCAN).
agent_test: Use as pilot design: N candidate rules, kill only on a failed example.

claim: Debate-style second views add little beyond voting when the views come from the same model; diversity of source (different models, +5.8 to +8.2%) and calibrated confidence are what help.
agent_test: The second rule must come from a different source or a tool, not from the same model asked to disagree.

claim: Casual pushback is a smaller risk for strong models than for small ones on debate stances (o3-mini 4.97 of 5 turns held, Qwen2.5-7B 0.83), and a third-person prompt or critic gate reduces flipping (up to 63.8% more turns held; 9.6% to 1.4% sycophancy for Claude Sonnet 4).
agent_test: Add pushback items; measure flips to wrong answers with and without a neutral-reviewer wording.

claim: Adding an opposite-role critic is not enough: in ReTAS, Dual View reflection was worse than Single View for GLM-4.6 and role swaps shifted attribution in over 20% of cases; training with thesis-antithesis-synthesis plus consistency reward made a 4B model beat larger open models.
agent_test: Include a perspective-swap consistency check in S7 rather than only a critic role.

claim: No replication with N>=300 per culture of the 1999 contradiction-plausibility task and no 30-60 item rerun of the LLM Dialectical Self Scale was found; the one direct replication (proverbs) failed.
agent_test: Do not depend on the human effect size; run an own pilot.
